claims.text: The identity of X controls whether a stable, coherent protective oxide persists on CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C.
Diffusion kinetics of X govern protective-scale formation and persistence.
Oxidation thermodynamics of X govern protective-scale formation and persistence.
Si forms thermodynamically stable, low-mobility SiO2 under the stated conditions.
Al forms thermodynamically stable, low-mobility Al2O3 under the stated conditions.
Si or Al produces gradual, balanced outward diffusion that promotes a continuous, adherent oxide scale.
The oxide scales promoted by Si or Al have low growth stress.
Mn forms less-stable and faster-growing oxides than Si or Al.
Mn-bearing scales mismatch the substrate chemically and mechanically.
Chemical and mechanical mismatch in the Mn-bearing scale causes cracking or spallation.
Mn promotes a rapidly forming, porous oxide with high growth stress.
Interphase boundaries in multiphase alloys may alter localized diffusion and oxide-scale formation.
At 950 °C for 100 hours, Si- or Al-bearing alloys will form thinner and more slowly growing oxide scales than the Mn-bearing alloy.
At 950 °C for 100 hours, Si- or Al-bearing alloys will form more uniform and better-adherent oxide scales with fewer defects than the Mn-bearing alloy.
The CrFeCoNiMn alloy is expected to produce an unstable, spall-prone oxide scale under the comparison conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Single-phase versus multiphase structure can modulate diffusion pathways and interfacial compatibility.
CrFeCoNiMn is designated as the controlled baseline for comparison with the Si- and Al-bearing variants.
